newsitem.title: UK: BAe climbs, GEC sinks on Thomson move.
newsitem.headline: BAe climbs, GEC sinks on Thomson move.

text.p: Shares in GEC Plc fell heavily but British Aerospace Plc advanced firmly after the French government named its preferred bidder for the privatisation of diversified electronics group Thomson SA on Wednesday.

BAe's shares climbed 13p to 11.26-1/2 stg and GEC's shares sank 10p to 388p on news that although both Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom's bids for the defence-to-media group would be considered, Lagardere's was the preferred offer.
Both British firms have many ties with each bidder and are set to benefit from the privatisation. But analysts say BAe could do better with its defence links with Lagardere's Matra.

In the first instance, BAe's most obvious point of contact with Thomson would be via its existing partnership with Matra on missiles, though no details of what an expanded link would involve were immediately available. Analysts said BAe's share price was unlikely to move much higher now as it was rumoured that Matra would probably join with Thomson's missiles division even if Lagardere's bid was unsuccessful.
"We thought it would be a consolation prize anyway," said the analyst, adding "...that was the only bit BAe was interested in."
"To me this (Lagardere) decision isn't industry consolidation," the analyst added. "You don't create a powerful world player by breaking off all the bits into joint ventures."
But he added the potential benefits for GEC were still apparent, although it seemed likely that the company would have to compete for involvement in various joint ventures.
"GEC will still benefit but there will not be the massive synergies had the whole lot gone in together...it is the worse of the two scenarios," the analyst said.
Another industry specialist, Michael Price of Arthur D Little, told Reuters Financial Television he saw the defence aspects of the Lagardere-led option in a more posititve light.
He said the alignment of Matra with Thomson-CSF had a bright outlook as it would give Matra much-needed scale and open the door for international partners to join in new alliances.
"It will probably become a magnet," he added.

Analysts said that GEC's existing Thomson-Marconi Sonar alliance, created in April this year and a dominant force in the world miltary sonar market, was unlikely to be affected by a Lagardere/Thomson deal.
GEC also has a 2.5 percent equity stake in Lagardere.
